How hard is it to buy weapons in US? I mean legally, don't you need some kind of license to use ?

Federally there is no license, except the Federal Firearm License (must be 21 years of age to get it) which is issued for dealers, brokers and manufacturers. It is for gun shops/manufacturing mostly, but others can get it to receive bulk stock/overseas shipments/more highly regulated arms. There are some weapons, like gatling guns, that require the owner or would-be owner to have an FFL.

Generally though, you simply must be at least 18 to buy.

However, that is federal. State laws vary greatly. I currently live in a state that has a license. I don't care for it, but if it gets to bugging me too much I can move. Some states have conceal carry licenses. Some have unlicensed conceal carry. Some are open carry. Some have different age requirements. Different handgun requirements.

So to answer your question. It isn't hard in most places. However, every purchase, except private sales (non-bulk, non-shop sales, like father to son, or brother to brother, but you still have to keep record of the sale.) requires a federal background check, so every commercial purchase requires the presentation of ID.
